Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
733 AM EDT Sat Oct 17 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 310 AM EDT Saturday...

No significant changes were made with this forecast package.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 310 AM EDT Saturday...

1. Snowfall is expected for portions of the mountains above 
1500-2000 feet this morning, then widespread gusty winds and cold 
temperatures continue today before a moderating trend begins early 
next week.

2. The long term is very quiet with comfortable temperatures 
and dry conditions prevailing for the upcoming week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 310 AM EDT Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: As rainfall becomes more showery in the wake of the cold 
front, the northwesterly flow regime will support upslope rain 
and/or snow showers across the western slopes of the Adirondacks and 
Green Mountains. Locations above 2000 feet continue to look like the 
best spots for up to an inch of snow accumulation while a few 
flurries could be seen as low as 1500 feet. Overall impacts will be 
minimal and likely confined to grassy surfaces as the ground 
temperatures will remain above freezing this morning. Today will be 
quite the transition to a more winter-like pattern as temperatures 
struggle to climb into the upper 30s to mid 40s while winds remain 
gusty in the 20 to 30 mph range, especially this morning. This will 
lead to wind chills in the teens to mid 30s throughout the day with 
wind chills as low as the single digits above and below zero across 
the high peaks this morning. If you plan to be outdoors today, 
please dress and prepare for the weather as this dramatic cold and 
wind may be surprising to many! Tonight will be the coldest night of 
the week as winds finally abate and skies clear with lows falling 
into the upper teens and 20s. A rebound to more seasonal normal high 
temperatures is expected for Sunday through Tuesday as high pressure 
builds overhead with highs warming into the 50s and lower 60s, 
though nighttime lows should stay chilly in the 20s and 30s.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Mid/upper lvl ridge prevails through mid week, before 
weak cold front drops south acrs our cwa on Thurs with slightly 
cooler temps. The mid/upper lvl ridge acrs the NE CONUS, should keep 
moisture associated with coastal system well south of our cwa this 
week, which is supported by most 00z guidance and ensemble data. The 
weak cold frnt on Thurs has very limited moisture with best dynamics 
passing well north of our cwa, so have continued a dry fcst. A brief 
sprinkle or light shower is possible over the trrn with this 
feature, but confidence and probability is too low to mention attm. 
Given the dry conditions, warmer temperatures and sunshine, 
significant drying of fine fuels, including leaf litter can be 
anticipated this upcoming week, but winds are expected to remain 
light. High temps range from the mid 50s to mid 60s, except slightly 
cooler Thurs/Friday with lows upper 20s to lower 40s most mornings. 
No impactful or significant weather is anticipated this upcoming 
week or into next weekend attm.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Through 12Z Sunday...A few scattered mountain snow showers will
continue at times at SLK this morning with brief 15 to 20
minutes of IFR vis/cigs possible through 14z. Otherwise, a mix
of MVFR cigs in the mountain sites of MPV/EFK and SLK will
prevail until noon time, while mostly VFR at MSS/PBG/RUT and BTV
with maybe brief MVFR cigs at times this morning. Breezy
northwest winds 10 to 20 knots continues before becoming light
under 6 knots this evening and shifting to the south/southwest
by sunrise on Sunday with VFR at all sites expected. 

Outlook...

Sunday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Monday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Monday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.

&&

.MARINE...
A Lake Wind Advisory remains in effect for the broad waters and
southern waters of Lake Champlain this morning. Although the 
strongest winds have ended, we will continue to see 15 to 25 
knot winds across the lake, with gusts to 25-30 knots possible.
Winds are from the north and northwest this morning and should
gradually decrease throughout the day. Waves in the 3 to 5 ft 
range are expected this morning, subsiding to 1 to 3 feet this 
afternoon.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$
